lesson.content:
## What it is
Store-and-forward packet switching is a method of transmitting data packets through a network. In this method, a host sends a packet to the nearest router. The router stores the whole packet until it has arrived completely and its checksum is verified, then forwards it to the next router, until it reaches the destination. [p. 1]

## Real-life analogy
Imagine a post office where each letter is placed in a mailbox and then forwarded to the next mailbox until it reaches its final destination. Each mailbox acts as a router, storing the letter until it is fully processed and then forwarding it to the next one. [p. 1]

## How it works
1. The host sends a packet to the nearest router. [p. 1]
2. The router stores the whole packet until it has arrived completely and its checksum is verified. [p. 1]
3. The router forwards the packet to the next router. [p. 1]
4. This process continues until the packet reaches the destination router. [p. 1]
5. The destination router then forwards the packet to the final destination. [p. 1]

## Key terms
- **Router**: A device that stores and forwards packets until they reach their destination. [p. 1]
- **Checksum**: A value calculated from the data to ensure the data has not been altered during transmission. [p. 1]

## Example
Let's say you have a packet that needs to travel from Host A to Host Z. Host A sends the packet to Router 1. Router 1 stores the packet and forwards it to Router 2. Router 2 stores the packet and forwards it to Router 3, and so on until it reaches Router Z. Router Z then forwards the packet to Host Z. [p. 1]

## What to draw in the exam
No diagram needed. [p. 1]

## Exam tip
Examiners usually ask about the sequence of steps involved in store-and-forward packet switching. They look for a clear understanding of how packets are stored and forwarded through routers until they reach their destination. [p. 1]
